subject: Voicemod
title: Voicemod Alternatives in 2026
description: Eight Voicemod alternatives for streamers and gamers: mixers, noise removal, soundboards and AI voice services, with pricing models taken from vendor pages.
intro: Voicemod is a real-time AI voice changer and soundboard for PC and Mac. It is free to download, some functions and content sit behind a Voicemod PRO license or in-app purchases, and its home page advertises more than 200 voices. People who look past it usually want one narrower job done well: mixing several audio sources, removing background noise, routing a headset into a stream, or generating a synthetic voice. The eight tools below are grouped by that job, so the right replacement depends on what you actually use Voicemod for.
why_switch: The Voicemod terms of use say some functions and content need a PRO license or in-app purchases, so streamers who want a cost they can predict compare it against donationware and free tools.
A voice changer and a mixer are different jobs. Voicemeeter and Elgato Wave Link are built around routing and mixing audio sources, which Voicemod's voice-effect focus does not cover on its own.
Noise removal is its own category. Krisp and NVIDIA Broadcast describe noise cancellation or removal as a core function, which matters more than a funny voice for a call-heavy day.
Teams that need cloned or synthetic voices for production work look at ElevenLabs or Respeecher, which are built around voice models and APIs rather than a live effects bar.
Voicemod runs on PC and Mac. Anyone who needs Windows-specific tooling, or a hardware-linked tool from a headset or microphone maker, ends up on SteelSeries Sonar or Wave Link instead.

picks.name: Voicemeeter
picks.best_for: Free virtual audio mixing on Windows
picks.pricing: Donationware: free to use with all functions except optional features, with a license invitation after 30 days and five suggested amounts in the webshop.
picks.note: Voicemeeter is a mixer with a virtual audio device, not a voice changer, and that is the point. If your Voicemod setup mostly exists to route a microphone, a game and music into a stream, Voicemeeter does that routing with a pay-what-you-want model. You give up the preset voice library and gain a lot of control over which source goes where.

sources.fact: Voicemeeter is an audio mixer application with a virtual audio device used to mix and manage audio sources.
Voicemeeter is free to use with all functions available except optional features, under a donationware model.
The licensing page says the webshop proposes five different amounts for the donationware license.

picks.name: Elgato Wave Link
picks.best_for: Creators routing audio on Windows or Mac
picks.pricing: Free for Windows and Mac per the Wave Link 3.5 text; some effects plug-ins are sold separately on the Elgato Marketplace and are Windows only.
picks.note: Wave Link covers the routing side of a stream setup and adds a built-in soundboard in version 3.5, which overlaps with Voicemod's soundboard. Effects use VST3 on Windows and AU on macOS, so you bring your own plug-ins rather than a bundled voice catalog. Pick it if your pain point is balancing sources, not changing how you sound.

sources.fact: Wave Link is audio software built for creators, offering broadcast-level routing and effects.
Wave Link 3.5 adds a built-in soundboard, Smart Switch, Audio Flow and Wave Cast for dual-PC audio, and the page says it is free for Windows and Mac.
The page says effects use VST3 on Windows and AU on macOS.

picks.name: SteelSeries Sonar
picks.pricing: A free download button for Sonar LP is shown on the vendor page.
picks.note: Sonar is described as a way to raise or lower specific in-game sounds and shape the audio spectrum. That is a listening-side tool, where Voicemod works on what others hear from you. The page lists Windows 10 (RS5+) only, so Mac users are out. It suits players who care about hearing footsteps more than sounding like someone else.

sources.fact: The Sonar page describes it as a way to amplify or reduce specific in-game sounds and fine-tune the audio spectrum.
The page lists Windows 10 (RS5+) as the platform.
The page shows a free download button for Sonar LP.

picks.name: Krisp
picks.best_for: Noise cancellation for calls and meetings
picks.pricing: A free trial at $0 for 7 days; Core is listed at $8 and $16 per user per month, with the billing term unclear in the captured text.
picks.note: Krisp describes itself as voice AI for meetings, with noise cancellation and an AI note taker, and it sells an SDK for developers. It does not turn you into a character. Choose it when the job is clean speech in a work call or a collaborative stream, and be ready for per-user pricing instead of a one-time license.

sources.fact: Krisp describes itself as voice AI for meetings, with noise cancellation and an AI note taker.
The pricing page lists a Free Trial at $0 that is free for 7 days.
The pricing page lists Core at $8 and $16 per user per month, with the billing term of each price not clear in the extracted text.

picks.name: NVIDIA Broadcast
picks.best_for: Noise removal on Windows with NVIDIA hardware
picks.pricing: Pricing is not stated on the opened page; the app is offered as a download.
picks.note: The NVIDIA Broadcast app adds AI effects such as noise removal and a virtual background to livestreams, voice chats and calls. It lists Windows 10 and 11 64-bit and Windows on Arm. There is no voice-character library, so it replaces Voicemod only if you used it as a filter, not as a costume.

sources.fact: The NVIDIA Broadcast App adds AI effects such as noise removal and virtual background to livestreams, voice chats and video calls.
The page lists Windows 10 64-bit, Windows 11 64-bit and Windows on Arm as supported platforms.
Pricing is not stated on the opened Broadcast App page.

picks.name: MorphVOX
picks.best_for: Mac voice changing with extra packs
picks.pricing: Pricing is not stated on the opened home page.
picks.note: MorphVOX is the closest like-for-like swap in this list. Screaming Bee sells MorphVOX Mac as voice changer software for Macintosh computers and lists voice packs, sound effects and backgrounds as add-ons. Its site shows a 2005 to 2026 copyright, so it is a long-running product. Check the current price on the vendor site before switching.

sources.fact: Screaming Bee Software sells MorphVOX Mac, described on the site as voice changer software that runs on Macintosh computers.
The site also lists MorphVOX Voice Packs, Sound Effects and MorphVOX Backgrounds as products.
The site footer carries a 2005-2026 copyright for Screaming Bee Inc.

picks.name: ElevenLabs
picks.best_for: Synthetic voices and text to speech with an API
picks.pricing: Free at $0 per month with 10k credits; Starter $1 first month then $6; Creator $22 per month; Pro $99; Scale $299; Business $990; Enterprise custom.
picks.note: ElevenLabs offers text to speech, speech to text, voice cloning, dubbing and sound effects, with APIs and SDKs. It is a credit-metered web service rather than a live desktop effect, so it fits pre-recorded content, character voices for videos and bots. Expect to plan around credits, not a license.

sources.fact: ElevenLabs describes itself as an AI research and product company with three platforms: ElevenAgents, ElevenCreative and ElevenAPI.
ElevenLabs paid plans run from Creator at $22 per month after the first month to Business at $990 per month, with Enterprise on custom pricing.
ElevenLabs offers text to speech, speech to text, voice cloning, dubbing and sound effects, and provides APIs and SDKs for developers.

picks.name: Respeecher
picks.pricing: Marketplace plans at $18, $89 and $499 per month with discounted first months, plus a custom enterprise plan.
picks.note: Respeecher describes enterprise-grade voice cloning and synthetic speech for production work, with a voice marketplace and a Pro Tools plugin. Its about page says it was founded in Ukraine in February 2018. It is overkill for a casual stream, but it is the pick when a studio needs licensed AI voices for released content.

sources.fact: Respeecher's homepage describes enterprise-grade voice cloning and synthetic speech services for production work.
Respeecher's homepage lists a voice marketplace with a library of AI voices and a plugin for Pro Tools.
Respeecher's marketplace pricing page lists plans at $18/month, $89/month and $499/month, each with a discounted first month, plus a custom plan for organizations.

how_to_pick: Start with the single task you used Voicemod for last week. If it was costumes and soundboard clips, MorphVOX or the Wave Link soundboard are the nearest swaps. If it was juggling a mic, game and music, move to Voicemeeter or Wave Link. If viewers complained about background noise, Krisp or NVIDIA Broadcast solve that better. If the voice is for finished content, not a live session, look at ElevenLabs or Respeecher and budget by credits or plan tier.

faqs.q: Is there a free replacement for Voicemod?
faqs.a: Several tools here cost nothing to start. Voicemeeter is donationware, Wave Link is free for Windows and Mac per its 3.5 page text, and SteelSeries Sonar shows a free download. None of them copies Voicemod's voice library, so free here means a different tool for a different part of the job.

faqs.q: Which Voicemod alternative works on Mac?
faqs.a: Elgato Wave Link lists macOS with AU effects, and MorphVOX Mac is sold for Macintosh computers. Voicemeeter and SteelSeries Sonar are Windows tools per their pages, and NVIDIA Broadcast lists Windows only. Voicemod itself covers PC and Mac, so Mac users have fewer direct swaps.

faqs.q: Can I mix audio and change my voice with one program?
faqs.a: Not with a single tool in this list. Mixers such as Voicemeeter and Wave Link route sources, while MorphVOX changes the voice. Many streamers chain them, sending the voice changer's output into the mixer as one more input.

faqs.q: Are AI voice services a live voice changer?
faqs.a: ElevenLabs and Respeecher are described by their vendors around voice cloning, text to speech and production work. They are credit or plan based services, and their pages do not present them as a drop-in live effect for a game chat, so treat them as content tools.

faqs.q: What should I check before paying for any of these?
faqs.a: Read the current pricing page, since several vendors show first-month discounts or leave the price off the home page. MorphVOX and NVIDIA Broadcast did not state prices on the pages we opened, so confirm the cost directly.
